contrary_evidence: Euro adoption and TARGET/ECMS integration demonstrate institutional integration but do not by themselves demonstrate cheaper financing, persistent foreign inflows or durable equity-market depth.
MSCI Frontier reclassification demonstrates improved accessibility under MSCI criteria, not an investment endorsement or proof of sustained liquidity.
Fiscal and current-account deficits are forecast to widen while labour scarcity and wage pressure may constrain productivity gains.
A shallow domestic equity market means institutional accessibility may not translate quickly into market depth or broad foreign ownership.
limitations: Several economic effects of euro adoption and MSCI reclassification remain prospective and require post-adoption observations on spreads, flows, issuance, liquidity, productivity and real household incomes.
A single-day Bulgarian Stock Exchange turnover observation is illustrative of scale and is not a structural liquidity estimate.
Forecasts for 2026-2027 remain conditional on fiscal policy, energy prices, external demand and political decisions.
notes: Revision 2 resolves the prior QA blocking issues. The disputed NSI figures are now explicitly tied to the 3 July 2026 Key Indicators release and separated by statistical concept/reference period; causal language was narrowed; transmission mechanisms are explained in prose; and explicit falsifiers were added. No public bundle, HTML, data/reports.json or global site surface was created or changed by QA.

publication.revision_reason: QA factual and methodological corrections: reconciled NSI vintages, narrowed causal claims, expanded transmission mechanisms and strengthened explicit falsifiers.
qa_fixes_applied: Every NSI quantitative claim now names its reference period and dated release; national-accounts and balance-of-payments series are explicitly separated.
Observed institutional changes are separated from inferred effects on financing, flows, liquidity and productivity.
Transmission channels are explained in prose with mechanisms, conditions and countervailing responses.
The What would change our assessment section now contains explicit positive and negative falsifiers, including a direct falsifier of the institutional-transmission thesis.
EN and PT-BR were revised together for semantic equivalence.

selection_rationale.relevance: Euro-area membership changes Bulgaria's monetary, supervisory, payments and collateral architecture while altering its integration with European capital markets.
selection_rationale.change: The 2026 euro adoption, full Eurosystem infrastructure integration and MSCI move from Standalone to Frontier occur alongside a weaker fiscal trajectory, tight labour supply and a wider forecast external deficit.
selection_rationale.underattention: The country remains small in global portfolios and media coverage relative to the institutional and market-access changes now occurring.
selection_rationale.transmission: The transition links monetary institutions, fiscal policy, bank and capital-market access, wages, labour scarcity, housing, external balances and household purchasing power.

en.title: Bulgaria after euro adoption: institutional integration meets fiscal and labour constraints
en.deck: Euro adoption and MSCI reclassification have changed Bulgaria's institutional and market-access framework; the next test is whether fiscal dynamics, labour scarcity and shallow equity liquidity allow those changes to translate into productivity and durable market depth.
en.regime: Rapid institutional integration with low but rising public debt, tight labour supply and a shallow domestic capital market whose post-reclassification depth remains to be demonstrated.
en.key_risk: Nominal wage and spending convergence could outpace productivity and export capacity, leaving persistent fiscal and external imbalances despite stronger institutional integration.

pt-BR.title: Bulgária após a adoção do euro: integração institucional encontra restrições fiscais e de trabalho
pt-BR.deck: A adoção do euro e a reclassificação da MSCI mudaram o framework institucional e de acesso ao mercado; o próximo teste é saber se dinâmica fiscal, escassez de trabalho e baixa profundidade acionária permitirão transformar essas mudanças em produtividade e profundidade financeira duradoura.
pt-BR.regime: Integração institucional rápida, com dívida pública ainda baixa porém crescente, oferta de trabalho restrita e mercado doméstico de capitais cuja profundidade após a reclassificação ainda precisa ser demonstrada.
pt-BR.key_risk: A convergência nominal de salários e gastos pode avançar mais rapidamente que produtividade e capacidade exportadora, mantendo desequilíbrios fiscal e externo apesar da integração institucional mais forte.
